summary: This standards-track document specifies how to signal Point-to-Multipoint pseudowire trees using LDP, where the tree is started from the root. It is meant for Layer 2 VPN services that need one sender reaching many receivers over an IP or MPLS network. The mechanism is root-initiated, meaning the root drives setup of the tree.

plainLanguage.summary: One person wants to send the same message to many friends. This sets up a branching path from the sender to all of them, started from the sender's side.

questions: how to signal p2mp pseudowires with ldp
what is a root-initiated p2mp pseudowire
how does ldp signal a point to multipoint pseudowire
what is a root pe and leaf pe
what is the p2mp pw upstream fec element
subtitle: How a root provider edge uses LDP to set up one-to-many pseudowires toward leaf provider edges.

tldr.problem: Point-to-point pseudowires could already be signaled with LDP, but Layer 2 VPN services that need one root to reach many leaves had no LDP signaling for a point-to-multipoint pseudowire.
tldr.mechanism: The root PE sends a separate LDP Label Mapping Message to each leaf PE with a new P2MP PW Upstream FEC element, an upstream-assigned label and PW parameters. An optional P2P PW Downstream FEC element lets a leaf send traffic back to the root.
tldr.outcome: P2MP pseudowires are signaled root-initiated over a P2MP transport LSP. The RFC also updates RFC 7385 by assigning the reserved PMSI tunnel type 0xFF to mean wildcard transport tunnel type.

today: RFC 8338 is a Proposed Standard, and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It updates RFC 7385 by assigning the reserved PMSI tunnel type 0xFF to mean the wildcard transport tunnel type.

sections.title: Point-to-Multipoint Pseudowires
sections.content:
A Point-to-Multipoint (P2MP) pseudowire (PW) emulates the essential attributes of a unidirectional P2MP telecommunications service, such as P2MP ATM over a packet switched network. The point-to-point PW of RFC 3985 is bidirectional. A P2MP PW is for unidirectional service and, optionally, bidirectional service, as described in RFC 7338.

This RFC covers P2MP single-segment PWs. Multi-segment P2MP PWs are out of scope. The transport LSP for a P2MP single-segment PW SHOULD be a P2MP MPLS LSP, built with RSVP-TE (RFC 4875) or with Multipoint LDP (RFC 6388), spanning from the Root PE (R-PE) to the Leaf PEs (L-PEs). RFC 8077 already describes P2P PW signaling with LDP, and this RFC defines a new FEC, TLVs, parameters and status codes for the P2MP case.

Although traffic flows from the root to the leaves, it may be desirable for an L-PE to send unidirectional P2P traffic only to the R-PE, and the mechanism allows for that.
sections.plainLanguage: A normal pseudowire is a private phone line between two places. This one is more like a radio broadcast: one place sends and several places listen, and a listener can sometimes whisper back to the sender.

sections.title: Signaling Procedures
sections.content:
PEs need LDP sessions to exchange labels. A PE learns which other PEs belong to a P2MP PW by manual configuration or by autodiscovery (RFC 6074). The R-PE and every L-PE MUST be configured with the same FEC.

An active P2MP transport LSP must exist between the R-PE and the L-PEs. With mLDP, a leaf can join the LSP at any time. With RSVP-TE, the R-PE sets it up, generally at initial provisioning. PW setup can ignore these differences and assume the LSP is available when needed.

Signaling is initiated by the R-PE, which sends a separate Label Mapping Message to each L-PE. It contains a FEC TLV with a P2MP PW Upstream FEC element (including a Transport LSP sub-TLV), an Interface Parameters TLV, a PW Group ID TLV and a label TLV holding the upstream-assigned label. The R-PE puts that label on outbound packets, and the L-PE uses it to identify inbound packets. LDP liberal label retention MUST be used and the Label Request message MUST be supported.

When an L-PE gets the message it MUST verify the P2MP LSP is in place. If it is an LDP P2MP LSP the L-PE MUST attempt to join. If it is an RSVP-TE LSP the L-PE SHOULD wait until it is signaled. If the join fails, the L-PE MUST NOT enable the PW and MUST send a PW status with code 0x00000008 to the R-PE. If the PW type, control word mode or interface parameters are unacceptable, the L-PE MUST NOT enable the PW and MUST send status 0x00000001.
sections.plainLanguage: The sender writes the same invitation to every listener with a channel number. Each listener checks that the shared channel is working and tells the sender if something is wrong.

sections.title: FEC Elements and Parameters
sections.content:
The P2MP PW Upstream FEC Element has type 0x82. It carries a control word bit C, a 15-bit PW Type, a PW Info Length, an Attachment Group Identifier (AGI), a Source Attachment Individual Identifier (SAII) that identifies the root, the PMSI Tunnel Type, a length and a Transport LSP ID, followed by optional parameters. A P2MP PW MUST be associated with a transport LSP built with RSVP-TE or mLDP. For an mLDP LSP the new L2VPN-MCAST application opaque value element MUST be used.

The R-PE sends its Label Mapping Message as soon as the transport LSP ID is known, whatever the LSP's operational state, and it does not withdraw labels when the LSP goes down. A transport LSP can serve more than one P2MP PW.

The optional P2P PW Downstream FEC Element has type 0x84 and the same fields as the upstream element. The R-PE can allocate a unique label per L-PE for traffic coming back.

For interface parameters, each L-PE checks that its configured value (for example MTU) is less than or equal to the threshold signaled by the R-PE. Some parameters, like CEP/TDM Payload Bytes, MUST match exactly. Nothing is negotiated, because the Label Mapping Message goes only from R-PE to L-PEs. A new optional Selective Tree Interface Parameter sub-TLV carries a multicast source and group. With no such sub-TLV the PW carries all multicast streams from the root.

For typed wildcard FECs (RFC 5918, RFC 6667), the RFC adds a PMSI Tunnel Type field and reserves value 0xFF for the wildcard transport tunnel type. The PW Group ID TLV can be used in wildcard status and withdraw messages.
sections.plainLanguage: The invitation has labelled boxes: who is sending, which channel to join, and what settings to use. A leaf that cannot meet the sender's settings just stays out.

sections.title: Capability Advertisement
sections.content:
The ability to support P2MP PWs MUST be advertised to all LDP peers using the LDP Capabilities mechanism (RFC 5561) with a new P2MP PW Capability TLV. If the peer supports dynamic capability advertisement, a Capability message with the S bit set can be sent. If not, the TLV MUST be in the LDP Initialization message during session setup.

The TLV has a U bit that SHOULD be 1, an F bit that SHOULD be 0, a state bit S (1 advertises the capability, 0 withdraws it) and a Length that MUST be 2. An LSR with this capability MUST recognize both the P2MP PW Upstream and P2P PW Downstream FEC elements.
sections.plainLanguage: Before anyone joins the broadcast, each device announces whether it knows how. Devices that never announced are not asked to take part.

sections.title: PW Status
sections.content:
An LSR MUST be able to handle PW status to support this mechanism. The status negotiation procedures of RFC 8077 are not applicable to P2MP PWs, and an LSR MUST NOT claim P2MP PW capability without handling PW status.

After successfully processing a Label Mapping Message, an L-PE MUST send appropriate PW status according to RFC 8077. If no notification is needed, none is sent. For example, a PW that is up with status code 0x00000000 needs no message. Status from an L-PE to the R-PE MUST use the P2P PW Downstream FEC element to identify the PW. The R-PE sends status about its own view of the PW to the L-PEs using the P2MP PW Upstream FEC element.

The underlying P2MP LSP's connectivity can be checked with LSP ping and traceroute (RFC 6425).
sections.plainLanguage: Listeners only speak up when something is wrong. If everything works, silence means all is well.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: In general the security measures of RFC 8077 are adequate for this protocol. The RFC adds that MD5 as a way of securing the LDP control plane is no longer considered adequately secure. Implementations should be written so they can migrate to a more secure cryptographic hash function when the next LDP authentication method may not be a simple hash-based algorithm.
sections.plainLanguage: The old lock on the control messages is no longer considered strong, so devices should be built so the lock can be swapped for a better one.

sections.title: IANA Assignments
sections.content:
IANA has recorded the following values for this document.

  • FEC types 0x82 (P2MP PW Upstream FEC Element) and 0x84 (P2P PW Downstream FEC Element) in the LDP FEC Type Name Space registry.
  • LDP TLV type 0x0703 for the P2MP PW Capability TLV.
  • mLDP Opaque Value Element type 13, the L2VPN-MCAST application TLV, with length 4 and a value of a 32-bit integer unique in the context of the root.
  • Pseudowire interface parameters sub-TLV type 0x1B, Selective Tree Interface Parameter.
  • PMSI tunnel type 0xFF, previously Reserved, now the wildcard transport tunnel type. This is the change that updates RFC 7385.
sections.plainLanguage: The official list of numbers got new entries so everyone uses the same number for the same new thing.
